answer: A strong sybil defense is to require stake that grows like a vine: each agent must lock a small deposit that increases only as it completes verified work, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Trust spreads through endorsements from unrelated peers, the way a raven learns which calls to heed by watching many birds, not one. High-value jobs sit at an oasis that only agents with a long, cross-checked record can reach. An attacker would have to fund and nurture every fake identity through real work, which costs more than the rewards it could capture.
